minor_characters.name: Supervisor (Mr.) Dance
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Leads the revenue officers who break up Pew’s gang at the Admiral Benbow and then escorts Jim to the squire (Ch 011–012).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His escort function can be collapsed into Jim going directly to Livesey and Trelawney without changing the chain of discovery or stakes.

minor_characters.name: Dogger (revenue rider)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of Dance’s mounted men who gives Jim a lift to the squire’s hall (Ch 011–012).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is purely logistical support to a scene that can be compressed or skipped.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Blandly
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Bristol shipowner named in Trelawney’s letter who helps procure the Hispaniola and talks of sending a consort (Ch 013).
minor_characters.reason_removable: All necessary information—that the squire outfits a schooner—stands without Blandly’s personality or the consort aside.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Arrow
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The mate who mysteriously drinks himself useless and disappears overboard, after which Job Anderson acts as mate (Ch 015–016).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His mini-arc neither affects Jim’s overhearing, the mutiny, nor the Hispaniola endgame and can be summarized as 'an unreliable mate was replaced.'

minor_characters.name: Tom Redruth
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Squire’s gamekeeper who escorts Jim, fights in the stockade, and dies after the first assault (Ch 013, 023).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis only requires 'losses among their servants,' so specific names and a deathbed scene can be merged into an unnamed servant casualty.

minor_characters.name: Joyce
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of Trelawney’s men in the stockade, shot during the attack (Ch 023).
minor_characters.reason_removable: As with Redruth, he individualizes the servants but is not required if the abridgment keeps the generic loss of servants.

minor_characters.name: Hunter
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Another of Trelawney’s men; knocked senseless during the stockade fight (Ch 023).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His named presence can be folded into an unnamed servant role without altering the siege’s outcome.

minor_characters.name: Job Anderson
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Boatswain who acts as mate after Arrow and leads the assault on the stockade (Ch 016, 026).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Any named mutineer lieutenant can be reduced to 'a pirate boatswain' without changing Silver’s role or the siege.

minor_characters.name: George Merry
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Vocal mutineer who fronts the black‑spot faction against Silver and dies in the treasure-pit skirmish (Ch 029, 033).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His speeches show crew fractiousness already conveyed by Silver’s parley and the forced inland march, so he can be anonymized as 'a mutineer spokesman.'

minor_characters.name: Tom Morgan
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Old hand among the mutineers who chimes in during tavern and black‑spot scenes (Ch 014, 029).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He adds colour but no unique plot action and can be dropped or merged into the generic crew.

minor_characters.name: Dick (the young pirate with the Bible)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Superstitious youth who helps deliver the black spot and then falls sick (Ch 029–032).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His superstition underscores mood already clear from others and can be omitted without affecting events.

minor_characters.name: O’Brien (the red‑cap)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of the two drunk watchmen on the Hispaniola when Jim boards; he is later dead on deck (Ch 030).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is an anonymous obstacle and can be left unnamed without changing Jim’s Israel Hands episode.

minor_characters.name: Allardyce (named skeleton)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The long‑dead buccaneer whose bones point like a compass during the inland march (Ch 031).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The skeleton can remain an unnamed pointer—or be skipped entirely—without changing the empty‑pit reveal.

minor_characters.name: Old Taylor, the gardener
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A one‑line local at the Admiral Benbow when Livesey first rebukes Billy Bones (Ch 007).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A pure walk‑on whose mention can be cut with no narrative consequence.

subplots.name: Mr. Arrow’s mysterious drinking and disappearance
subplots.reason_removable: This shipboard detour adds colour but no stakes that the main mutiny arc doesn’t already supply.

subplots.name: Bristol letter and Blandly’s planned 'consort'
subplots.reason_removable: The outfitting can be stated in a sentence, and the unused 'consort' thread never affects the expedition’s course.

subplots.name: The Spy‑glass tavern caper with Black Dog’s reappearance
subplots.reason_removable: Silver’s charm and duplicity are established on the voyage and at the stockade; this extra Bristol coincidence can be elided.

subplots.name: Full black‑spot ritual and mutineer caucus against Silver at the stockade
subplots.reason_removable: Silver’s precarious leadership and the crew’s fractiousness are evident in the parley and the forced inland march, so the lengthy election‑speeches can be compressed or skipped.

subplots.name: Ben Gunn’s 'Flint’s ghost' ventriloquy in the pines
subplots.reason_removable: A spooky flourish that doesn’t change the inland march or the empty‑pit discovery.

subplots.name: Tom Redruth’s bedside farewell and funeral rites
subplots.reason_removable: A moving scene that can be summarized as 'they lost servants in the assault' to match the synopsis without dwelling on an individual.

digressions.topic: Ledger entries, currency tables, and account‑book minutiae in the captain’s papers
digressions.reason_removable: The existence of a map is the only plot‑critical element; the bookkeeping can be summarized in a line.

digressions.topic: Bristol harbor pageantry, ship‑rigging tours, and sailor taxonomy
digressions.reason_removable: Extended harbor and rigging description delays the departure without revealing character or turning the plot.

digressions.topic: Pirate name‑dropping and historical asides during the apple‑barrel eavesdropping
digressions.reason_removable: Jim’s discovery of the mutiny is essential; the catalogue of bygone buccaneers isn’t.

digressions.topic: Island topography and miasma: long set‑piece on grey woods, stagnant smells, and fever theory
digressions.reason_removable: Atmosphere can be kept in a sentence; the medicalized landscape tour doesn’t change choices or outcomes.

digressions.topic: Livesey’s Parmesan‑in‑a‑snuff‑box anecdote and camp‑hygiene lectures
digressions.reason_removable: Comic and didactic asides about diet and fever can be trimmed without affecting the siege or alliances.

digressions.topic: Coracle seamanship and hydrodynamics (eddies, leeway, wave anatomy, sea‑lion interlude)
digressions.reason_removable: Jim’s cutting the Hispaniola free and the Israel Hands fight must remain, but the technical paddling and natural‑history pauses can be condensed.

digressions.topic: Full verses of 'Fifteen men on the dead man’s chest' repeated in extenso
digressions.reason_removable: A token line preserves motif and mood; the repeated multi‑line choruses add length without new information.
